sections.h2: Where is Carroll County, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Carroll County is in central Maryland on the Piedmont Plateau, with Pennsylvania to the north, Howard County to the south, Baltimore County to the east and Frederick County to the west. Westminster is the county seat, and the county belongs to the Washington-Baltimore combined statistical area.

It covers 453 square miles, almost all of it land, and the terrain is rolling hills and deciduous forest with Parr's Ridge running southwest to northeast. Liberty Reservoir and Piney Run Reservoir are the two existing reservoirs.

The county was created in 1837 from parts of Baltimore and Frederick Counties and named for Charles Carroll of Carrollton. Eldersburg is the largest community, and the 2020 census counted 172,891 residents, with a 2025 estimate of 176,677.

sections.h2: What does the Carroll County economy look like?
sections.html:
Schools, health care and government lead the employer lists. In Westminster itself, Carroll County Public Schools has 3,757 employees, McDaniel College 641, the county government 593, Carroll Lutheran Village 437 and General Dynamics Robotics Systems 350.

Just outside the city limits, Carroll Hospital Center is the largest employer at 1,696 workers, and Random House follows with 800. McDaniel College and Carroll Community College are both in Westminster.

Total taxable base matters here too. The state's fiscal analysts show Carroll County's assessable base at about $27.4 billion for fiscal 2026 and a projected $29.1 billion for fiscal 2027. The base grows as assessments rise, which is one reason bills can climb even when a rate holds still.

sections.h2: What is the Carroll County property tax rate?
sections.html:
The county rate is $1.018 per $100 of assessed value and the state adds $0.112, for $1.130 per $100 outside any town. A house with a $400,000 taxable assessment would owe about $4,520 before credits, using our own arithmetic.

Eight towns add their own rates, and the combined figures vary a lot, so the town you live in changes your bill more than most owners expect.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 reassessment affect Carroll County?
sections.html:
Carroll's residential full cash value rose 16.1% between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026, which was well above the 13.2% statewide residential average for the group. Assessment notices went out on December 30, 2025.

Increases are phased in evenly over three years, while decreases take effect immediately. For an owner-occupied home, the homestead credit limits annual increases in taxable value to 5% in the county, and the cap is set by each town, so Mount Airy is 3% and Sykesville and Taneytown are 10%.

Maryland assessment appeals start with the state's local assessment office, which for Carroll is at 15 East Main Street in Westminster according to the county's tax bill notes. The usual first deadline is 45 days from the notice date.

sections.h2: When are Carroll County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Full-year taxes and the first semi-annual installment are due July 1 and can be paid without interest through September 30. The second installment is due December 1 and can be paid without interest through December 31.

Discounts apply to full-year payments only: 1% if paid by July 31 and 0.5% if paid by August 31. Semi-annual payments do not earn a discount, and a service charge applies to the second installment unless both are paid by September 30.

  • Full-year and first-installment bills become delinquent on October 1.
  • The second installment becomes delinquent January 1.
  • The county says interest and penalties will not be waived for any reason and due dates will not be extended.
  • A pending appeal or tax credit application does not change the due date.
  • Not receiving a bill does not excuse nonpayment, so request a duplicate.

These dates come from the county's tax bill notes for the tax year beginning July 1, 2024, so check the current bill for any changes.

sections.h2: How does the Carroll County tax sale work?
sections.html:
The county sells liens on unpaid real estate tax in an online sale run through RealAuction each June. For 2025 the notice said proceedings started April 1, and the sale was held June 30.

Starting May 1, delinquent taxes must be paid by cash, certified check or money order, and additional fees apply. Owners who wait until late April or May lose the card and online options.

Paying the current year does not protect you from legal action for unpaid prior years, according to the county. A Homeowner Protection Program page is linked from the Collections Office, so ask about eligibility if you are close to the sale.

sections.h2: How do you pay, and who do you call?
sections.html:
The Collections Office is on the first floor of the county building at 225 N. Center Street in Westminster, open Monday through Thursday 8 am to 5 pm and Friday 8 am to 3 pm. The phone number is 410-386-2971.

  • Online or by phone with a card: a vendor fee applies, listed as 2.5% on cards and $1.50 for an e-check.
  • By mail: PO Box 3237, Westminster, MD 21158-3237.
  • Drop box: open around the clock in the lower parking lot outside the building.
  • Cash or check: accepted at Carroll County Public Library branches.

Credits worth asking about include the county Senior Tax Credit for homeowners 65 and older, a $15,000 assessment exemption for legally blind owners and a full exemption for veterans with a 100% service-connected permanent disability. Qualifications differ, so call before assuming you are eligible.

sections.h2: What roads and weather shape a Carroll County house sale?
sections.html:
Maryland Route 140 is the main road, running from Baltimore through Westminster toward Taneytown. Route 97 is the most direct way south toward Washington, and Routes 27 and 31 link nearby towns. Westminster has no inter-county bus or rail service to Baltimore County, so most residents drive.

The county sits on a line between humid subtropical and hot-summer humid continental climates. Westminster averages about 43 inches of precipitation and 20 inches of snow a year, which puts steady demands on roofs, gutters and heating systems.

Westminster itself was founded in 1764 and incorporated in 1818, and Corbit's Charge was fought on its streets on June 28, 1863. Its older downtown housing is a very different product from the newer subdivisions around Eldersburg.

sections.h2: What should a Carroll County seller do about tax at closing?
sections.html:
1. Pull the bill and find out which installment, if any, is unpaid.
  2. Ask the Collections Office for a payoff and for the status of any lien.
  3. Tell your lender if taxes are escrowed so they are not paid twice.
  4. Give the title company a payoff request well before closing.

If the house is behind on tax, needs repair or both, selling as-is for cash can clear the balance from the proceeds at settlement.

faqs.q: What is the Carroll County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is $1.018 per $100 of assessed value, plus $0.112 for the state, for $1.130 per $100 outside a town. Town rates are added where they apply.

faqs.q: Which Carroll County town has the highest total rate?
faqs.a: Westminster, at $1.6900 per $100 combined according to the state's 2026 to 2027 table. Mount Airy has the lowest town total at $1.3262.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Carroll County tax early?
faqs.a: Yes, for full-year payments only: 1% by July 31 and 0.5% by August 31, per the county's tax bill notes for the 2024 tax year. Semi-annual payments get no discount.

faqs.q: When is the Carroll County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is held online each June. The 2025 sale was on June 30, with cash, certified check or money order required from May 1.

faqs.q: How much did Carroll County assessments rise in 2026?
faqs.a: Residential full cash value rose 16.1% from January 1, 2023 to January 1, 2026. Increases are phased in over three years.

faqs.q: Does Carroll County let owners defer or reduce tax?
faqs.a: It offers a Senior Tax Credit, a Homeowner Protection Program and state credits, plus exemptions for blind owners and disabled veterans. Each has its own qualifications, so call the Collections Office.
